record.original_question: How far is D_mu(M), the Frechet Lie group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms with the right-invariant L2 hydrodynamic metric, from being an infinite-dimensional locally symmetric Riemannian space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth Riemannian manifold equipped with a smooth volume form $\mu$. Let $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$ denote the Fréchet Lie group of smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$, endowed with the right-invariant weak Riemannian metric induced at the identity by the $L^2$ inner product on divergence-free vector fields:
$$\langle u, v\rangle = \int_M \langle u(x), v(x)\rangle_{g}\,d\mu(x),$$
for $u,v \in T_e\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$. With respect to this metric, geodesics on $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$ correspond (via Arnold's principle) to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$. Let $R$ denote the sectional curvature tensor of this weak Riemannian structure on $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$.

Recall that a Riemannian manifold (in the finite-dimensional sense) is locally symmetric if and only if $\nabla R \equiv 0$, where $\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita connection. Extending this notion to the infinite-dimensional Fréchet setting, quantify in a precise sense the extent to which $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$, equipped with the right-invariant $L^2$ hydrodynamic metric, fails to be a locally symmetric Riemannian space. In particular, characterize (or estimate) the covariant derivative $\nabla R$ of the curvature tensor, identify obstructions to local symmetry, and determine for which manifolds $M$ (if any) the space $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$ is locally symmetric.
artifact.category_tag: Infinite-dimensional Riemannian geometry of diffeomorphism groups
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found. The question is posed as an open problem in the geometric hydrodynamics literature, and searches reveal active related research on the curvature and geometry of volume-preserving diffeomorphism groups but no result determining how far $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$ is from being locally symmetric.

status_evidence.title: Volume-Preserving Diffeomorphism Groups (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the L2 right-invariant metric on volume-preserving diffeomorphism groups and Arnold's framework, without addressing local symmetry.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference confirms the geometric setup but does not resolve the local symmetry question.

status_evidence.title: The L2-metric on the space of smooth maps
status_evidence.snippet: Studies L2 metrics on mapping spaces and their curvature properties.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on the L2 geometry exists but does not settle local symmetry of $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$.
